thread:
maria gomez: quick brain dump — i think we need to pick a default tradeoff for the continuous batcher: do we favor latency hedging (speculative small batches) or cohort simplicity (coalesce aggressively, accept occasional tail). microbursts and small requests are the main pain.
jon paulson: leaning hedging for interactive routes. customers care about p95 and interactive UX. hedging reduces tail but costs more GPU cycles.
li zhang: +1 for route-level defaults. hedging messes with kv-cache locality though — more small batches == worse cache hit rate. example config i've been testing:
```
hedging.enabled = true
hedging.max_speculative_size = 3
coalesce.window_ms = 12
kv_cache.prefetch = true
```
pranav singh: hybrid could work: let a policy decide per-route: if latency_target < 150ms -> hedging, else cohort. also expose a cost_sensitivity flag so SMs can prefer cheaper behavior.
maria gomez: ops question — how do we detect when hedging is doing net harm? need telemetry: per-route batch_size_histogram, wait_time_ms, evicted_batches, kv_miss_rate, tokens_per_gpu_sec.
sre-bot: ALERT: interactive-prod: batcher.wait_time_p95 exceeded 200ms for 3m
jon paulson: that alert means our hedging thresholds might be too aggressive (waiting to form small speculative batches). Could be a misconfig on the route or a change in request size distribution.
li zhang: right. simulation showed hedging improves p95 for synthetic small messages, but when payload variance increases kv-cache churn drops hit rate by ~18% causing downstream slowdowns.
pranav singh: operationally: offer two knobs to users: latency_target_ms and cost_sensitivity. Runtime translates into admission and coalesce heuristics. keeps UX simple and internal mapping flexible.
maria gomez: love that pattern — keep surface small. Action items: i'll sketch an RFC with mapping table + required metrics and an escape hatch (force-coalesce route flag).
jon paulson: i'll add perf numbers from the last canary and a short script to replay microburst traces against the simulator.
li zhang: i'll run kv-cache churn simulations and measure p50/p95 delta for hedging vs cohort in our repo's sim harness.
pranav singh: suggest including 'soft_min_batch' + hysteresis instead of hard min to avoid starvation when many small low-priority requests come in.
maria gomez: noted. volunteers to review RFC? timeline: draft by EOD Wed, review Thurs.
jon paulson: i can review Thurs morning.
li zhang: Thurs afternoon works for me.
pranav singh: :thumbsup: will add the hysteresis notes.
maria gomez: thanks all — i'll post RFC link here when ready. small follow-up: can we add a lightweight dashboard tile for batch_size vs kv_miss_rate? that's the most direct signal.
jon paulson: agreed, will prototype a grafana panel.
li zhang: if panel exists we can run A/B on a canary and watch expected improvement metrics.
pranav singh: ok cool. closing here until RFC posted.
